samples.summary: New test asserts only that some callback invocation saw 'heading:2'; it never checks the callback's arguments or fire count
samples.evidence: The test pushes a string derived from `editor.getBlockType()` (a fresh read of editor state) and asserts `seen).toContain('heading:2')`. It never inspects the `(pos, selection)` arguments passed by the new `notifyStyleApplied()` call, which passes `undefined` for the selection whereas `afterCursorRender` (editor.ts:2039) passes `null` — that divergence in the new notification path is untested. It also does not assert the number of fires, so an accidental duplicate notification (render path + explicit notify) would go unnoticed.

samples.summary: The Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+2 test exercises no code the diff changed, so it adds no coverage for the fix despite being presented alongside it
samples.evidence: The shortcut path in text-editor.ts:1023-1036 calls `this.doc.setBlockType(...)` then `this.requestRender()` (wired to `renderWithScroll`, editor.ts:2102), which already called `afterCursorRender()` → `fireCursorMoveCallbacks` before this diff. The test therefore passes identically with or without the added `notifyStyleApplied()` at editor.ts:2811. Valid as a regression pin, but it must not be read as coverage of the change.

samples.summary: Pre-existing 'dispose drops all listeners' test is vacuous — it asserts a call count is unchanged without triggering any post-dispose fire
samples.evidence: After `editor.dispose()` the test asserts `cb.mock.calls.length).toBe(callsBeforeDispose)` with no intervening action that could fire callbacks, as its own comment concedes ("We can't easily trigger a fire post-dispose"). The assertion holds whether or not dispose actually clears `cursorMoveCallbacks`; e.g. removing the clear in `dispose` would not fail it. Not introduced by this diff, but it sits directly beside the new tests in the same suite.

samples.summary: Only the heading case of the changed `setBlockType` API is covered; list/paragraph transitions are not
samples.evidence: The new test calls `editor.setBlockType('heading', { headingLevel: 2 })` only. `setBlockType` (editor.ts:2802) also accepts `paragraph` and list kinds/levels, which the toolbar control reads through the same `getBlockType()`. Same single code path, so value is low, but no test exercises the non-heading arguments.
